questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with multiple hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk and limbs with thickened peripheral nerves. Slit skin smear shows AFB. What is the most appropriate treatment regimen?
opts: WHO MDT for paucibacillary leprosy (6 months)
WHO MDT for multibacillary leprosy (12 months)
questions.exp: A positive slit skin smear (AFB) classifies this as multibacillary leprosy regardless of the number of patches, requiring WHO MDT-MB regimen (rifampicin + clofazimine + dapsone) for 12 months.

questions.q: A 22-year-old sexually active woman presents with a single painless ulcer on the labia majora with a clean base and indurated edges. The ulcer does not bleed on probing. Which investigation is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?
opts: Dark field microscopy of ulcer exudate
Gram stain for Gram-negative intracellular diplococci
questions.exp: The description is classic for primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre): painless, indurated, clean-based ulcer. Dark field microscopy demonstrating Treponema pallidum spirochetes from ulcer exudate is the gold standard for diagnosis of primary syphilis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a rapidly spreading erythema and tenderness of the scrotum and perineum with crepitus on palpation. He is diabetic. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a synergistic necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum and genitalia. The combination of rapid spread, crepitus (gas-forming organisms), scrotal/perineal involvement, and diabetes mellitus is characteristic.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with a painless chronic ulcer on the foot with black granules in the discharge. Microscopy shows broad septate hyphae. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Eumycetoma (black grain mycetoma) caused by Madurella mycetomatis is treated with oral itraconazole. The black grains and broad septate hyphae help identify this as eumycetoma rather than actinomycetoma.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child develops multiple fluid-filled blisters on the face and extremities that rupture easily to form honey-coloured crusts. The most common causative organism is:
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (or mixed infection with Streptococcus). The honey-coloured crusts result from dried serous exudate following rupture of superficial vesicles/pustules.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with tense blisters on normal and erythematous skin, predominantly in the flexures. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is characterized by tense blisters (subepidermal) on normal or urticarial skin in flexural areas. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. The target antigen is BP180 (type XVII collagen).

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with flaccid blisters involving the oral mucosa and scalp. Nikolsky sign is positive. Histology reveals acantholysis in the suprabasal layer. Which antibody is responsible?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris predominantly involves mucous membranes and shows anti-desmoglein 3 antibodies (mucosal type). When both skin and mucosa are affected, both anti-Dsg1 and anti-Dsg3 are present. Suprabasal acantholysis is characteristic.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive at 1:320 with anti-dsDNA positive. Which skin finding is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.exp: The malar (butterfly) rash is characteristic of SLE, sparing the nasolabial folds and appearing after sun exposure. While discoid lesions occur in SLE, they are more specific for discoid lupus erythematosus. The malar rash in the context of systemic features is most specific for SLE.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 80 cells/μL) develops painless violaceous plaques on the legs and oral cavity. Biopsy shows proliferating spindle cells and slit-like vascular spaces. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma in AIDS is caused by Human Herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8, KSHV). It presents with violaceous plaques and nodules in AIDS patients with low CD4 counts. Histology shows spindle cells and slit-like vascular spaces filled with red cells.

questions.q: A 60-year-old fair-skinned farmer presents with a slow-growing, pearly, rolled-edge nodule with central ulceration and telangiectasias on the nose. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (rodent ulcer) classically presents as a pearly, translucent nodule with a rolled border, central ulceration, and surface telangiectasias on sun-exposed areas. It is the most common skin malignancy, occurring on the face (especially nose) in fair-skinned individuals.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with itchy, grouped vesicles on erythematous bases over the elbows, knees, and buttocks. IgA deposits are found at the dermal papilla tips on DIF. Which associated systemic condition must be evaluated?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis is the cutaneous manifestation of coeliac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy). DIF shows IgA deposits at dermal papilla tips. Treatment involves gluten-free diet and dapsone.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with well-defined silvery-white plaques on the scalp, elbows, and knees with nail pitting. The Auspitz sign is positive. What is the pathological basis of Auspitz sign?
opts: Loss of granular layer leading to easy desquamation
Dilated capillaries in elongated dermal papillae bleeding on scale removal
questions.exp: Auspitz sign (bleeding after scale removal in psoriasis) occurs because thinning of the suprapapillary epidermis exposes dilated, tortuous capillaries in elongated dermal papillae. Minimal trauma ruptures these vessels.

questions.q: A patient on methotrexate for psoriasis develops mouth ulcers and macrocytic anaemia after 3 months. What is the mechanism and management?
opts: Direct mucosal toxicity; switch to cyclosporine
Folate deficiency due to DHFR inhibition; add folic acid supplementation
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), depleting tetrahydrofolate needed for DNA synthesis and leading to folate deficiency symptoms (oral ulcers, macrocytic anaemia, GI toxicity). Folic acid 5 mg/day (given on non-MTX days) prevents toxicity without reducing efficacy.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops a targetoid lesion on the hand, with a dusky centre, edematous middle ring, and erythematous outer ring following herpes labialis. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythema multiforme minor is characterized by typical target (iris/bull's eye) lesions with three zones on acral sites, commonly triggered by HSV. It has minimal mucosal involvement. SJS has >2 mucous membrane sites affected and epidermal detachment <10% BSA.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with comedones, inflammatory papules, and pustules on the face. He is started on oral isotretinoin. Which of the following monitoring parameters is most important?
opts: Liver function tests and fasting lipid profile
questions.exp: Isotretinoin can cause elevated liver enzymes (hepatotoxicity) and hypertriglyceridemia. Baseline and monthly monitoring of LFTs and fasting lipid profile is mandatory. Teratogenicity requires pregnancy testing in females before and during treatment.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, calcinosis cutis, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. The ANA pattern is centromeric. What antibody is most specifically associated?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis) is associated with anti-centromere antibody (ACA). Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and carries a worse prognosis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man from Tamil Nadu presents with a painless scrotal swelling with woody induration and lymphedema of the leg. Nocturnal blood samples show microfilariae. The most effective drug for treatment is:
questions.exp: Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti) causing elephantiasis is treated with diethylcarbamazine (DEC) citrate. DEC acts against both microfilariae and adult worms. WHO recommends DEC + albendazole (or ivermectin + albendazole in Africa) for mass drug administration.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with a cluster of painful vesicles on an erythematous base along the T4 dermatome on the right side of the chest. He had chickenpox at age 5. Diagnosis and first-line treatment?
opts: Herpes zoster; oral acyclovir 800 mg 5 times/day for 7 days
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (shingles) results from reactivation of VZV in dorsal root ganglia. It presents with dermatomal vesicles on erythematous base. Oral acyclovir 800 mg 5 times daily for 7 days (or valacyclovir/famciclovir) is the first-line antiviral treatment.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with multiple soft, smooth, dome-shaped papules with central umbilication on the face. The lesions have increased over 3 months. The causative poxvirus is:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (MCV, a poxvirus) causes characteristic umbilicated pearly papules. In immunocompromised patients (HIV, CD4 <200), lesions are numerous, large, and may involve the face atypically. The hallmark is central umbilication containing molluscum bodies.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with multiple flesh-coloured papules at the introitus and perianal region. Acetowhitening is positive on application of 5% acetic acid. Which HPV subtypes are most commonly responsible?
questions.exp: Condyloma acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by low-risk HPV subtypes 6 and 11. High-risk types 16 and 18 are associated with cervical and anogenital carcinomas. HPV 1 and 2 cause plantar and common warts.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painful genital ulcer with undermined edges, ragged base, and associated inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo) that is tender. Gram stain shows 'school of fish' arrangement of Gram-negative rods. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Chancroid caused by Haemophilus ducreyi presents with painful genital ulcers with ragged, undermined edges and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Gram stain shows Gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' pattern.

questions.q: On Wood's lamp examination of a patient with tinea versicolor, the affected areas show which characteristic fluorescence?
questions.exp: Tinea versicolor (Malassezia furfur) shows yellow-green or gold/copper-orange fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Coral red fluorescence is seen in erythrasma (Corynebacterium minutissimum). Bright green is seen in some dermatophyte infections.

questions.q: A 4-year-old girl develops diffuse red skin with superficial exfoliation in sheets following a fever. The child appears toxic. Nikolsky sign is positive. Blood culture grows Staphylococcus aureus. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B of phage group II Staphylococcus aureus. It mainly affects neonates and young children, causing superficial blistering and exfoliation. Histology shows cleavage in the granular layer (unlike TEN where cleavage is subepidermal).

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with progressive symmetric proximal muscle weakness and a heliotrope rash with periorbital oedema. Gottron's papules are seen over the knuckles. The malignancy most commonly associated with this condition is:
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis in adults is associated with underlying malignancy in 15-30% of cases. In women, ovarian cancer is the most commonly associated malignancy. In men, lung and colorectal cancers are more common. Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis requires thorough malignancy screening.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing pigmented nodule on the back that bleeds on touch. Dermoscopy shows blue-white veil, irregular streaks, and atypical pigment network. The Breslow thickness on biopsy is 2.5 mm. What is the significance of this measurement?
opts: Most important prognostic factor determining surgical margins and sentinel node biopsy
questions.exp: Breslow thickness (vertical depth from granular layer to deepest tumour cell) is the single most important prognostic factor in melanoma. It determines surgical excision margins and the need for sentinel lymph node biopsy. >1 mm Breslow thickness warrants SLNB.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with an intensely itchy, violaceous, flat-topped polygonal papule on the flexor wrist with white lacy pattern (Wickham striae). The T-lymphocyte-mediated pathology targets:
opts: Basal keratinocytes at the dermoepidermal junction
questions.exp: Lichen planus is a T-lymphocyte-mediated (CD8+ cytotoxic) disorder targeting basal keratinocytes at the dermoepidermal junction, causing the characteristic band-like lichenoid infiltrate on histology. The 5 P's: Pruritic, Purple, Polygonal, Planar, Papules.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with progressive diffuse hair loss with widening of the central part. Trichoscopy shows miniaturized hairs and reduced hair density at the vertex. Serum ferritin is 8 ng/mL. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Female pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia in women) presents with diffuse thinning at the vertex and widening of the central part, sparing the frontal hairline. Trichoscopy confirms miniaturization. Low ferritin can exacerbate FPHL and should be corrected.

questions.q: A patient with vitiligo is being started on narrowband UVB phototherapy. What is the proposed mechanism of repigmentation?
opts: Destruction of residual melanocytes in affected skin
Stimulation of outer root sheath melanocyte reservoir to proliferate and migrate
Induction of immune tolerance to UV radiation
Direct synthesis of melanin by keratinocytes
questions.exp: NB-UVB phototherapy promotes repigmentation in vitiligo by stimulating melanocyte precursors (melanoblasts) in the outer root sheath of hair follicles to proliferate, differentiate, and migrate to the epidermis. This explains why follicular repigmentation (perifollicular pattern) is seen first.

questions.q: During patch testing for allergic contact dermatitis, a patient develops a +2 reaction. How is this graded and what does it indicate?
opts: Erythema, oedema, papules; definite allergic reaction
Vesicles beyond the patch area; extreme allergic reaction
questions.exp: ICDRG grading: + (doubtful, faint erythema), ++ (erythema, infiltration, papules; definite positive), +++ (erythema, infiltration, vesicles), ++++ (bullae and spread beyond patch). A ++ reaction indicates a definite allergic contact sensitization to the tested allergen.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with multiple pigmented macules on the palms, soles, and oral mucosa. He also has polyps in the small intestine and has lost significant weight. What is the most likely associated genodermatosis?
questions.exp: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (autosomal dominant, STK11/LKB1 mutation) presents with mucocutaneous lentigines (lips, oral mucosa, palms, soles) and hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps. There is increased risk of GI malignancy and extra-intestinal cancers.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with episodic flushing, diarrhoea, and bronchospasm. On examination, she has telangiectasias and erythema of the nose and cheeks. Urinary 5-HIAA is elevated. What skin diagnosis should be considered?
questions.exp: Carcinoid syndrome (from metastatic carcinoid tumour) causes episodic flushing, diarrhoea, and bronchospasm due to serotonin excess, confirmed by elevated urinary 5-HIAA. The flushing can resemble rosacea. Niacin deficiency (pellagra) from tryptophan diversion can co-occur, causing photosensitive dermatitis.
